additional_info.subject: Re: 0391015 - ID0391015-DC/Si-D/FR-[Y2 / R6 313033014001] Charing Session Stops CRM:00658000827
additional_info.body:
Dear Malek,
Thank you for your prompt response.
We understand that the charging session is already enabled to start when OCPP is offline; however, in this case, it did not initiate because OCPP was online. This process only works when the charger is offline before starting the charging session, or more accurately, before authorization.
In this particular charging session, the session stopped because the charger did not receive a response for the
StartTransaction
message.
During offline charging, authorization is managed directly by the charger, without requiring backend communication. This explains why offline charging did not initiate and why the online charging session failed in this instance.
Proposal to Address the Issue
To prevent similar issues in the future, we recommend increasing the default timeout period for OCPP messages from
15 seconds
to
30 seconds
. This would allow the charger to wait longer for a response from the backend before terminating the session. If no response is received within the extended period, the session will still terminate.
Please let us know if we have your permission to increase the default timeout for OCPP messages to 30 seconds. Also, feel free to reach out if you have any further questions.
We look forward to your response.
Best Regards,
Sominath Nagalgaon
eMobility Support Team
Please do not change the subject line with replying back to this email.

Dear Malek Drif,

I have reviewed the additional logs of the charger and can confirm that this vehicle successfully charged on this unit.

additional_info.body:
Good evening,
Thank you for your message.
You mentioned that the truck charged successfully last night, but here’s the full story that you may not know. After observing the issue, I was fortunate to notify Mr. HERBRICH, who was still in his office at the time. He personally took care of unplugging and reconnecting the truck to restart the charging session.
Last year, we already went through a stressful winter dealing with this type of issue. On several occasions, someone from his team had to intervene, even very late at night, sometimes for hours. It became exhausting and demoralizing for the drivers, and we don’t want to face the same chaos again this year.
As you know, these trucks are not V2G-compatible, and we don’t encounter this kind of problem with other charger models. It’s crucial to urgently deploy the update that can interpret the BCB toggle as a WakeUp function.
If restarting the charger is indeed a solution, as you suggested, I give you full authorization to proceed immediately.
We remain vigilant and especially attentive to the commitments made by your management over the past two years.
Best regards,
